LESSON: WATER

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: RESOURCES IN OUR ENVIRONMENT Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Sugges
Topic 3.1: Water
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 13

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Water, part of RESOURCES IN OUR ENVIRONMENT Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Sugges in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we use water without wasting it? 2. Why do we care for water sources?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Water together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Unity: Learners enrich equality as they display team spirit when they participate in school water day to share experiences on using water

sparingly.

● Respect: Learners enhance acceptance of their peers when they appreciate their diverse opinions as they think, pair and share

experiences on careful use of water in the home and school.

● Responsibility: Learners enhance resilience as they engage activities involving careful usage of water and re-using water.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Health promotion issues- Health and hygiene awareness is enhanced as learners drink clean water and role play using water sparingly

for personal wellbeing.

Link to other Learning Areas:

● Creative Arts: Sources of water in the immediate environment can develop the skill of modelling.

● English Activities: Sources of water in the immediate environment can be used to develop the skills of listening/observing,

speaking/signing.

Suggested Learning Resources

Adapted learner’s books, digital devices, crayons, pencils, captioned and signed audio visual clips, picture cards, pictures sign cards,
